purpose: Primary documentation review for prospective D2 design; no native or installed-candidate execution evidence.

facts: Python handlers execute in the main interpreter main thread and only that thread installs handlers.
A handler-raised exception can interrupt Python execution at an arbitrary bytecode boundary.
SIGKILL cannot be caught, blocked or ignored.
sources.review_obligation: Signal handlers must not acquire application locks or invoke session cleanup; interrupted acquisition cannot be treated as atomic.

facts: Thread.join returns None; checking is_alive after a successful join determines whether timeout occurred.
Uncaught thread exceptions normally reach threading.excepthook and may print to stderr.
Daemon threads may be abruptly stopped at interpreter shutdown.
sources.review_obligation: Use non-daemon handles, no success on join return alone, preserve uncertainty after failed/interrupted join, sanitize target exceptions without raw traceback.

facts: Termination of a PID namespace init process causes kernel SIGKILL of the namespace processes.
Namespace init has special signal handling restrictions; ancestor SIGKILL and SIGSTOP are exceptions.
sources.review_obligation: Do not equate cooperative signal handling with hard host-owned termination or infer native liveness from a fake hold seam.

facts: For covered EINTR cases, returning signal handlers permit retry with timeout recomputed; raising handlers propagate.
os.close and os.dup2 are special: EINTR is ignored rather than retrying the syscall.
sources.review_obligation: Do not retry uncertain close; retain exact ownership and separate logical checks from physical evidence.

facts: The script directory and user site are excluded from sys.path; PYTHON environment variables are ignored.
sources.review_obligation: Use installed app plus explicitly pinned source loading, no path injection; candidate runtime admission remains separate.

scope: Documentation informs review only. Holds, signals, imported resource footprint and actual cleanup still require tests and later physical admission; no new code or deployment here.
